entities.name: Engagement Lift Measurement Framework
entities.description: An A/B testing framework designed to measure the impact of in-stream ads on engagement for MCC videos distributed through the Genuin carousel, comparing monetization gains against engagement degradation.

entities.name: Genuin Carousel
entities.description: A Genuin-hosted placement on partner sites that displays MCC videos and serves as the unit of measurement for impressions, clicks, and video starts in the experiment.

entities.name: MCC Videos
entities.description: Video content uploaded by MCC to Genuin and distributed via the Genuin carousel, serving as the content pool tested for ad-supported vs no-ads engagement.

entities.name: MCC
entities.description: Content partner that uploads videos to Genuin and places the Genuin carousel on its site; the business stakeholder whose engagement and monetization goals shape the test thresholds.

entities.name: In-Stream Ads
entities.description: Pre-roll or mid-roll ads delivered inside MCC videos via VAST requests in the Treatment variant of the test.

entities.name: Control Variant (No Ads)
entities.description: Experiment arm where the player does not send a VAST request and content starts immediately when the user plays a video.

entities.name: Treatment Variant (Ads)
entities.description: Experiment arm where the player issues a VAST request on play and serves an in-stream ad before or during content when fill is available.

entities.name: VAST
entities.description: Video Ad Serving Template protocol used by the Genuin player to request and render in-stream ads from the ad server.

entities.name: Ad Server
entities.description: Backend system that responds to VAST requests with ad creatives and is the source for fill rate, response time, and creative metadata.

entities.name: Genuin Video Player
entities.description: Client player that loads videos, fires VAST requests, plays ads and content, and emits the experiment's tracking events such as video_start, content_start, and ad_impression.

entities.name: Revenue per Eligible Session
entities.description: Primary monetization KPI defined as total ad revenue divided by eligible sessions, used to assess the commercial impact of enabling in-stream ads.

entities.name: Average Watch Time per Eligible Session
entities.description: Primary engagement KPI defined as total content watch time divided by eligible sessions, capturing actual consumption and indirect ad friction.

entities.name: Completion Rate
entities.description: Guardrail engagement KPI equal to content_complete divided by content_start, monitored to ensure ads do not collapse video completion.

entities.name: Content Start Rate
entities.description: Funnel KPI equal to content_start divided by video_start; isolates how often actual editorial content begins after a play attempt.

entities.name: Carousel CTR
entities.description: Funnel KPI equal to carousel item clicks divided by carousel impressions, measuring upstream interest in the carousel.

entities.name: Video Start Rate
entities.description: Funnel KPI equal to video_start divided by carousel_impression, capturing how often carousel views convert into play attempts.

entities.name: Ad Request Rate
entities.description: Ad funnel KPI equal to ad_request divided by video_start, indicating how often eligible plays trigger a VAST call.

entities.name: Ad Fill Rate
entities.description: Ad funnel KPI equal to filled ad_response divided by ad_request, reflecting ad server supply for the test inventory.

entities.name: Ad Impression Rate
entities.description: Ad funnel KPI equal to ad_impressions divided by video_starts, showing how often a video start produces a valid ad exposure.

entities.name: Ad Completion Rate
entities.description: Ad KPI equal to ad_complete divided by ad_start, measuring how often started ads play to completion.

entities.name: Ad Error Rate
entities.description: Quality KPI equal to ad_error divided by ad_request, used as a technical guardrail for ad delivery health.

entities.name: Revenue per Content Start
entities.description: Monetization KPI equal to total ad revenue divided by content_start, isolating revenue per actual content consumption event.

entities.name: eCPM per 1,000 Eligible Sessions
entities.description: Monetization KPI computed as (total ad revenue / eligible sessions) × 1000, expressing revenue intensity per thousand sessions.

entities.name: Videos per Session
entities.description: Engagement KPI equal to total content starts divided by eligible sessions, capturing breadth of consumption per visit.

entities.name: Exit Rate after Play Start
entities.description: Guardrail engagement metric equal to video_exit after video_start divided by video_start, flagging abandonment driven by ad friction.

entities.name: Lift Formula
entities.description: Standard A/B readout calculation Lift % = ((Treatment / Control) - 1) × 100, applied to revenue, watch time, and completion KPIs.

entities.name: Decision Rule
entities.description: Framework rule that launches Ads broadly only if revenue/session lifts significantly while watch time, completion, and quality stay within acceptable thresholds.

entities.name: Event Tracking Schema
entities.description: Practical event model defining identity join keys (experiment_id, variant_id, session_id, etc.) and core carousel, player, ad, and revenue events for the experiment.

entities.name: carousel_impression
entities.description: Event fired when the Genuin carousel is rendered or viewable per the agreed measurement rule, carrying carousel, placement, page, and viewability properties.

entities.name: carousel_item_click
entities.description: Event fired when a user clicks or taps a video tile in the carousel, with video_id, item_position, content_category, and thumbnail_type properties.

entities.name: video_player_load
entities.description: Event fired when the player initializes, carrying video_id, player_id, autoplay, muted, and player_size properties.

entities.name: video_start
entities.description: Event fired when playback starts from user intent, with start_type indicating click, autoplay, or similar trigger.

entities.name: content_start
entities.description: Event fired when actual editorial content begins; distinct from video_start in ad-supported flows so engagement loss is not hidden.

entities.name: content_progress
entities.description: Event fired at 25%, 50%, and 75% milestones with progress_pct and watch_time_seconds properties.

entities.name: content_complete
entities.description: Event fired when content reaches the completion rule, carrying watch_time_seconds and completion_pct.

entities.name: video_exit
entities.description: Event fired when a user exits the player or page before completion, with exit_reason and watch_time_seconds.

entities.name: ad_request
entities.description: Event fired when a VAST call is sent, carrying ad_server, ad_unit_id, request_id, ad_position, and timeout_setting_ms.

entities.name: ad_response
entities.description: Event fired when the ad server responds, with fill_status, creative_id, advertiser, campaign_id, and response_time_ms.

entities.name: ad_impression
entities.description: Event fired when an ad impression is validly served, carrying creative_id, campaign_id, ad_duration_seconds, and skippable flags.

entities.name: ad_start
entities.description: Event fired when ad playback begins for an in-stream ad in the Treatment variant.

entities.name: ad_complete
entities.description: Event fired when an in-stream ad finishes, carrying ad_watch_time_seconds.

entities.name: ad_skip
entities.description: Event fired when a user skips a skippable ad, with skip_offset_seconds.

entities.name: ad_error
entities.description: Event fired on ad playback or render failure, with error_code and error_message properties.

entities.name: ad_revenue
entities.description: Event fired when revenue is attributed, carrying revenue_amount, currency, pricing_model, creative_id, and campaign_id.

entities.name: Experiment Guardrails
entities.description: Rules that exclude bots, internal QA traffic, broken placements, sessions with missing assignment or mid-session variant flips, and require sticky assignment and parallel run dates.

entities.name: Segmentation Plan
entities.description: Plan to cut the analysis by device, geography, traffic source, page template, new vs returning users, placement position, content category, player size, and connection quality.

entities.name: New vs Returning Users
entities.description: User segment dimension used in the analysis to assess differential ad friction impact between new and returning visitors.

entities.name: Device Segment
entities.description: Mobile, desktop, and tablet split used to compare ad friction impact across device classes.

entities.name: Geography Segment
entities.description: Geographic cut (country) applied to engagement and revenue comparisons across variants.

entities.name: Traffic Source Segment
entities.description: Cut of traffic by acquisition source used to detect source-specific ad friction or monetization patterns.

entities.name: Dashboard Layout
entities.description: Recommended reporting layout with Executive Summary, Funnel View, Segment View, and Quality View tiles for the A/B readout.

entities.name: Executive Summary View
entities.description: Top-level dashboard tile showing revenue/session, watch time/session, completion rate, net lift %, and decision status across variants.

entities.name: Funnel View
entities.description: Dashboard view tracing impression → click → video start → ad start → content start → completion across variants.

entities.name: Quality View
entities.description: Dashboard view monitoring ad errors, buffering, timeout rate, and player failures as technical guardrails.

relationships.description: The framework measures the impact of in-stream ads on engagement for videos served through the Genuin carousel.
The test specifically evaluates engagement and monetization tradeoffs for MCC video content.
The framework's thresholds and business goals are set in collaboration with MCC as the content partner.
MCC uploads its own video content that is distributed through the Genuin carousel.
MCC places the Genuin carousel on its site to surface MCC videos to its audience.
The carousel surfaces MCC-hosted videos to end users on partner sites.
Defines the No Ads control arm where playback begins without any VAST request.
Defines the Ads treatment arm where a VAST request is fired on play to serve in-stream ads.
The treatment arm enables in-stream ads before or during MCC video content.
Treatment variant relies on VAST requests issued by the player to fetch ads.
In-stream ads are delivered through VAST protocol requests and responses.
VAST requests are sent to and answered by the ad server.
The Genuin player issues VAST requests on play when ads are enabled.
The player renders pre-roll or mid-roll in-stream ads inside MCC videos.
The player emits the carousel, content, ad, and revenue events defined by the tracking schema.
Carousel item clicks instantiate the Genuin video player to begin playback.
Schema defines carousel_impression as the carousel render/viewability event.
Schema defines carousel_item_click for user clicks/taps on carousel video tiles.
Schema defines video_player_load for player initialization.
Schema defines video_start as the user-intent playback event.
Schema defines content_start to mark when editorial content actually begins.
Schema defines content_progress milestones at 25/50/75%.
Schema defines content_complete for content completion.
Schema defines video_exit for early exits with reason and watch time.
Schema defines ad_request to mark outgoing VAST calls.
Schema defines ad_response with fill status and creative metadata.
Schema defines ad_impression for validly served ad exposures.
Schema defines ad_start for ad playback initiation.
Schema defines ad_complete for ad finish events.
Schema defines ad_skip for skip interactions on skippable ads.
Schema defines ad_error for ad playback or render failures.
Schema defines ad_revenue for revenue attribution events.
Revenue/session is computed from ad_revenue events aggregated over eligible sessions.

relationships.source: Average Watch Time per Eligible Session
relationships.description: Average watch time is derived from content_progress and related watch-time signals over eligible sessions.
Completion rate is computed from content_complete events relative to content_start.
Completion rate uses content_start as its denominator.
Content Start Rate is content_start divided by video_start.
Content Start Rate uses video_start as its denominator.
Carousel CTR uses carousel_item_click as its numerator.
Carousel CTR uses carousel_impression as its denominator.
Video Start Rate uses video_start as its numerator over carousel impressions.
Video Start Rate uses carousel_impression as its denominator.
Ad Request Rate uses ad_request events over video_starts.
Ad Fill Rate uses filled ad_response events as numerator.
Ad Fill Rate uses ad_request as its denominator.
Ad Impression Rate uses ad_impression events over video_starts.
Ad Completion Rate uses ad_complete over ad_start.
Ad Completion Rate uses ad_start as its denominator.
Ad Error Rate uses ad_error events over ad_request.
Revenue per Content Start aggregates ad_revenue over content_start events.
Revenue per Content Start uses content_start as its denominator.
eCPM per 1,000 eligible sessions is computed by scaling revenue per eligible session by 1000.
Exit Rate after Play Start uses video_exit events following video_start.
Videos per Session is computed as total content_start events divided by eligible sessions.
The decision rule launches ads only if revenue per eligible session lifts significantly.

relationships.target: Average Watch Time per Eligible Session
relationships.description: The decision rule requires that watch time per eligible session remain within an acceptable decline threshold.
The decision rule requires that completion rate not materially collapse.
The decision rule monitors content start rate to ensure no material drop-off in actual content consumption.
Lift Formula is applied to revenue per eligible session to compute monetization lift.

relationships.target: Average Watch Time per Eligible Session
relationships.description: Lift Formula is applied to average watch time per eligible session to compute engagement lift or drop.
Lift Formula is applied to completion rate to compute completion lift or drop.
Defines Revenue per Eligible Session as the primary monetization KPI.

relationships.target: Average Watch Time per Eligible Session
relationships.description: Defines Average Watch Time per Eligible Session as the primary engagement KPI.
Includes Completion Rate as a guardrail KPI.
Includes Content Start Rate as a guardrail KPI.
Includes Exit Rate after Play Start as a guardrail KPI.
Includes Carousel CTR among secondary funnel metrics.
Includes Video Start Rate among secondary funnel metrics.
Includes Ad Request Rate among ad funnel metrics.
Includes Ad Fill Rate among ad funnel metrics.
Includes Ad Impression Rate among ad funnel metrics.
Includes Ad Completion Rate among ad funnel metrics.
Includes Ad Error Rate as a quality KPI.
Includes Videos per Session as a secondary engagement metric.
Includes Revenue per Content Start as a secondary monetization metric.
Includes eCPM per 1,000 Eligible Sessions as a monetization KPI.
The framework relies on the tracking schema to produce the events feeding its KPIs.
Defines exclusion and integrity guardrails that protect the validity of the comparison.
Specifies cuts of analysis by device, geography, traffic source, page template, and more.
Specifies the recommended decision rule for launching, iterating, or holding ads.
Defines the Lift % formula used in readouts.
Recommends the dashboard layout used to communicate the readout.
The dashboard layout includes an Executive Summary tile for top-line KPIs and decision status.
The dashboard layout includes a Funnel View tracing impression-to-completion.
The dashboard layout includes a Quality View for ad and player errors and buffering.
Segmentation includes device type cuts (mobile/desktop/tablet).
Segmentation includes geography (country) cuts.
Segmentation includes traffic source cuts.
Segmentation includes new vs returning user cuts.
Guardrails rely on tracking schema fields like experiment_id and variant_id to detect missing assignment or mid-session flips.
